flawed_step: A unique minimum cut does not rule out independently variable circulations in maximum flows.
counterexample: Let V={s,u,v,t}. The arcs and integer capacities are s→t:1, u→t:1, v→t:1, u→v:1, and v→u:1. The four s-t cuts have capacities: cap({s})=1; cap({s,u})=3; cap({s,v})=3; cap({s,u,v})=3. Thus {s} is the unique minimum cut. One maximum flow sends 1 on s→t and 0 on every other arc. A distinct maximum flow sends 1 on each of s→t, u→v, and v→u, and 0 on u→t and v→t. Both are feasible and have value 1, which is maximum because the cut {s} has capacity 1.
assessment_summary: The network has exactly four vertices and a unique minimum cut, but it has distinct maximum flows differing by a circulation on the antiparallel arcs u→v and v→u.
